notesStmt.note: This manuscript was created between June 4, 1887, the date of the letter on which it is written, and January 29, 1888, when it appeared in the Herald.
"Halcyon Days" was first published in the 29 January 1888 issue of the New York Herald. It was later included in November Boughs (1888).

lg.l: O for the happy and quiet days!
The teeming and blissful halcyon days!
When will they come? and where do they rise?
Do they come Not from successful love? alone,

Nor wealth, nor ‸honors'd in middle age, nor victories
of politics or war

But As life wanes ‸(submitting, adjusting itself and submits —)—as the sea of the turbulent
passions is calmesd
As the gorgeous and silent colors of sunset cover the ‸evening west sky

As that an indescribable softness and rest
suffuses the spirit and frame, like
a fresher, balmier air,

l.add:
As the ‸shortening days life takes on a mellower light and the apple
hangs finished and ended and ripe on the tree

lg.l:
E'en as the winter solstice is passing
or passed, and night ‸duly approaches,
Then for the happyiest and quietest days ‸of all!
The teeming ‸and brooding and blissful halcyon days!
